data.body:
Live Bedrock proof (session experiment, AWS us-east-1, model bedrock:us.anthropic.claude-sonnet-4-6):

- physical_context_ceiling(verifier model) = 2,000,000 chars (window-derived: sonnet own window 1,000,000 tokens x 2 chars/token), NOT the old flat 100,000.
- The live c9f7 shape (assembled context 121,147 chars x 22 criteria; product 2,665,234) is ADMITTED past _validate_recovery_inputs preflight (no CompletionRecoveryError). The retired flat _MAX_CONTEXT_CHARS=100,000 bound would have REFUSED it at preflight (121,147 > 100,000).
- A live Bedrock evidence run over a 115,000-char (>100,000) context returned a verdict in one request: usage input_tokens=25,050, output_tokens=20, requests=1, finish_reason=stop, elapsed ~3.8s. Recovery reaches a verdict rather than refusing at preflight.

Conclusion: a completion verification whose assembled context exceeds 100,000 chars completes bounded recovery past preflight to a verdict under the window-derived ceiling, satisfying the live-Bedrock AC.
